newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Japan, EU call for closer economic, political ties.
newsitem.headline: Japan, EU call for closer economic, political ties.

text.p: The European Union and Japan ended their sixth annual summit on a high note on Wednesday, endorsing trade and financial developments and pledging closer political links.
"This was an excellent summit conducted in a good atmosphere," said European Commission President Jacques Santer. "We have a powerful political alliance that is always growing."
Santer was speaking after talks in The Hague with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutoro Hashimoto and Wim Kok, the Dutch Prime Minister who also holds the EU's rotating presidency.
They discussed matters ranging from European economic and monetary union (EMU) and Japan's trade surplus to African development and the situation in Cambodia.
But the most substantive item to emerge from the one-day summit was a decision to accelerate work on a mutual recognition agreement (MRA) treaty to facilitate bilateral trade.
Both sides agreed to try before next year's summit for an MRA similar to those initialled last week by the EU with the United States and Canada.
An MRA will allow manufacturers from both sides to test and certify products once only, at home, rather than have to repeat the exercise in the country to which they are exported.
The initial MRA will cover pharmaceuticals, medical devices, electromagnetic components and certain electrical and telecommunication equipment.

Hashimoto also said that from September this year, Japan would allow imports of certain medical devices under a so-called "good manufacturing principles" scheme by which Japan recognised the standards to which certain European products have been made.
EU officials stressed their concern at Japan's continuing trade surplus, but Hashimoto assured them that his government believed a recent increase was not a trend.
He urged the EU to step up efforts to encourage its companies to seek investment opportunities in Japan and stressed there was genuine domestic reform under way that would help.

The EU also reiterated that it wanted to see more effort made to deregulate Japan's complex and tightly-controlled distribution system which often sees European products struggling for recognition in the Japanese market.

Both sides also welcomed work being done by the World Semiconductor Council and the World Trade Organisation, and called for an early conclusion to the Multilateral Agreement on Investment to help facilitate global trade.
On political links, both sides said they wanted to strengthen ties -- particularly in cooperating in the developing world.

Japan, due next year to host an international conference on development in Africa, said it would particularly like closer cooperation on food aid, human resources for aid organisations and support for education and health programmes.
On China, both sides welcomed efforts by Beijing to meet conditions for WTO membership, but stressed that reforms should be genuine.
They also urged China to ensure a smooth and peaceful transition of Hong Kong to mainland rule at the end of the month.
Japan and the EU also called on political leaders in Cambodia -- rocked recently by factional fighting -- to work for stability and reiterated their support for peace in Bosnia and the Middle East.
